The gate buzzes because Green must go in after Blue.
The gate clicks open on their first try!

accepted.title: The Carrom Clue
accepted.text:
At their cousin's house, Kavya posts a riddle in the cousins' group chat to find the carrom board:

'It is kept in either the study, the veranda, or the storeroom. It is on the ground floor, but not in any room that has a fan.'

Karthik checks the rooms:
• The study is upstairs.
• The veranda has a ceiling fan.

Where did Kavya put the carrom board?

options.consequence: Karthik heads upstairs, but the study is on the first floor.
Karthik checks the veranda, but the whirring ceiling fan rules it out.
Karthik opens the storeroom door and finds the carrom board leaning against the shelf.

hint.text: Which room meets both conditions: downstairs and without a fan?

puzzle.explanation: The study is upstairs, so it cannot be the room. The veranda has a fan, which eliminates it. That leaves only the storeroom.

grade.rationale: This straightforward logic puzzle requires two steps of elimination to rule out the study and veranda. Because it is a purely cognitive reasoning puzzle, no SEL competencies are scored. The correct location is the storeroom.

The hint nudges effectively without giving away the answer, and the explanation is clear and kind.

accepted.title: Sprint Timings
accepted.text: At sprint practice, four runners timed their laps. Divya wore blue and Mehul wore red; the other two runners wore green and yellow. Looking at the coach's board: Divya finished ahead of Mehul. Mehul did not finish last. The runner in third place wore green. Who finished in second place?

options.consequence: Divya was ahead of Mehul, placing her in first.
Mehul eliminates third and last place, leaving him in second.
The board confirms the runner in green took third.
Yellow ended up taking fourth place.

hint.text: Rule out which positions Mehul cannot possibly be in.

puzzle.explanation: Mehul wore red, so he was not third (green). He was not fourth (last). Because Divya was ahead of him, he cannot be first either. That leaves Mehul in second place.

grade.rationale: Mehul cannot be 4th (stated) or 3rd (3rd place wore green, whereas Mehul wore red). Since Divya finished ahead of Mehul, Mehul cannot be 1st either, leaving 2nd place for Mehul. This requires two logical elimination steps appropriate for middle school students.

accepted.title: Flashlight lineup in the dark
accepted.text:
During a sudden power cut at home, Karthik and Ravi line up four flashlights in a row on the table from left to right: Amber, Blue, Green, and Red.

• The Red flashlight is at an outer end, but not the far right.
• The Amber flashlight is placed directly between Red and Blue.
• The Blue flashlight sits to the left of the Green flashlight.

Which flashlight is in the third position from the left?

options.consequence: Amber sits second, right between Red and Blue.
Karthik clicks the third switch and a bright blue beam cuts through the dark.
Green must sit at the far right end in fourth place.
Red is placed first on the far left.

hint.text: Find where Red must go first, then check which flashlights must flank Amber.

puzzle.explanation: Since Red is at an end but not on the far right, Red is first. Amber sits between Red and Blue, placing Amber second and Blue third. Green goes fourth, keeping Blue to its left.

grade.rationale: This logic puzzle uses straightforward deductive steps suitable for ages 11-14. By placing Red at the far left (position 1), Amber directly next in position 2, and Blue in position 3, the third position is clearly identified as Blue.

reasons: Clear, engaging logic puzzle set in a relatable everyday context (a power cut).
Hints and explanations are gentle, step-by-step, and mathematically sound.
Consequences for incorrect choices clarify the logic kindly without shaming.

accepted.title: Slippers by the Door
accepted.text: At his cousin's house, Rahul lines up four pairs of slippers: blue, red, yellow, and green. The green pair is at the far right. The red pair is right next to green. The blue pair is not next to red. Which pair is at the far left?

options.consequence: Rahul places the blue slippers right at the far left.
The red slippers must sit beside the green ones instead.
The yellow pair fits into the second spot beside red.
The green slippers are already at the far right.

hint.text: Where does the green pair go first, and who can sit next to red?

puzzle.explanation: Green is in spot 4 and red is in spot 3. Because blue cannot touch red, blue must go to spot 1 at the far left.

accepted.title: The Festival Mystery Bags
accepted.text:
At the colony festival celebration, Nikhil and Harsh stand before a game stall. Three gift bags—Blue, Orange, and Green—sit on the counter. Exactly one bag contains the prize token.

The tags read:
• Blue bag: "The token is not in this bag."
• Orange bag: "The token is not in the Green bag."
• Green bag: "The token is in this bag."

The stallkeeper smiles: "Only one tag tells the truth; the other two are false."

Which bag contains the token?

options.consequence: Nikhil opens the Blue bag and pulls out the shining prize token!
If the token were in Orange, both Blue and Orange tags would be telling the truth.
If the token were in Green, both Blue and Green tags would be telling the truth.
Testing each bag one by one reveals a single logical answer.

hint.text: Test each bag one by one. If the token were in that bag, how many tags would be true?

puzzle.explanation: If the token is in Orange or Green, Blue's tag is automatically true, making at least two tags true. Only if the token is in Blue is exactly one tag true: Orange's.

grade.rationale: To solve this logic puzzle, children must evaluate the truth value of each tag. Since the Orange tag ('not in Green') and Green tag ('in Green') are direct opposites, exactly one of them must be true. Because only one tag overall is true, the Blue tag ('not in Blue') must be false, meaning the token is in the Blue bag.

reasons: A clean, well-constructed logic puzzle that fits the established house style.
The reasoning is logically sound and the explanation is clear and respectful.
The colony festival setting is relatable and culturally natural for Indian children.
